intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Day Hike
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's Great Walks, this iconic 19.4km hike traverses volcanic terrain, emerald lakes, and dramatic landscapes. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown to maximize daylight hours. Ideal for experienced hikers seeking breathtaking alpine scenery without wasting arrival day logistics.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett in the Nevis Valley. Located just 45 minutes from central Queenstown, this is the ultimate adrenaline experience. Book in advance to secure a morning slot and combine with nearby accommodation in Queenstown to avoid long transfers.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-renowned Great Walk spanning 32km through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Stay at huts along the trail to avoid costly transfers. Book hut passes well in advance. Starting from Glenorchy, just 45 minutes from Queenstown, this minimizes travel time and maximizes trail days.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungy site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, located just 23km from central Queenstown. A historic and accessible experience perfect for first-timers or those wanting a shorter transfer. Combine with a riverside café lunch nearby to make the most of the afternoon.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise
experiences.description: Combine a guided hike along the Milford Track day walk with a scenic cruise through Milford Sound's dramatic fiords and waterfalls. Depart from Te Anau (2.5 hours from Queenstown) and stay overnight in Te Anau to avoid a rushed same-day return. This keeps costs low while delivering maximum natural impact.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungy site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, located just 23km from central Queenstown. A historic and accessible experience perfect for first-timers or those wanting a shorter transfer. Combine with a riverside café lunch nearby to make the most of the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, grab a local SIM card at the airport, and take the Connectabus (budget-friendly ~NZD $10) to central Queenstown. Check in to Queenstown Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a leisurely self-guided walk along the Queenstown lakefront and Earnslaw Park to get your bearings. Enjoy views of The Remarkables mountain range across Lake Wakatipu - completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through central Queenstown and explore the buzzing town centre. Head to Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution, budget-friendly ~NZD $15-18 for a burger) for dinner - arrive before 18:00 to beat the queue. Afterwards, walk up to the free Queenstown Hill viewpoint lookout near the town centre for sunset views over the lake.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pie from a bakery or Four Square supermarket near the airport or town centre (~NZD $5-8)
meals.dinner: Fergburger, central Queenstown - massive, legendary burgers at reasonable prices (~NZD $15-18)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a free Queenstown map at the i-SITE visitor centre on Shotover Street. Download the MetService NZ weather app to track conditions for hiking days. Buy groceries at Countdown supermarket for budget breakfasts and lunches throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the accommodation, then tackle the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui). This free 2-3 hour return hike starts just 10 minutes walk from the town centre. The trail rises 500m above Queenstown offering panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Start by 08:00 to enjoy cooler morning temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Queenstown Hill and head to the Queenstown Gardens (free entry) for a relaxing picnic lunch on the grass. Explore the rose gardens and disc golf course. In the mid-afternoon, walk the free Frankton Track along the lakeside (~6km one way) or rent a bike from Hire A Bike Queenstown (~NZD $25 half day) to cycle the full Queenstown Trail section along the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and browse the Queenstown Night Markets (if Monday - check schedule) on O'Connell's Shopping Centre carpark. Pick up cheap street food from various vendors (~NZD $8-12 per dish). Alternatively, cook a simple pasta or stir-fry at the accommodation using supermarket supplies to save money.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Self-packed sandwiches and fruit eaten as a picnic in Queenstown Gardens (~NZD $4-6)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food stalls (~NZD $10-15) or self-catered at accommodation (~NZD $5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for Queenstown Hill. Carry at least 1.5L of water per person. The track can be muddy after rain - check conditions. Queenstown Hill takes approximately 2.5-3 hours return at a moderate pace.

day_by_day.morning: THE BIG ADVENTURE DAY - Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump! Take the Shotover Jet shuttle or a rideshare (~NZD $10-15 each way) to the Kawarau Bungy Centre, 23km from Queenstown. This is the world's first commercial bungy site, perched 43 meters above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River gorge. Book in advance online for the best price (~NZD $165-185). Watch others jump while you wait, then take the plunge! The experience includes free viewing of your jump from the bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Walk the free Queenstown Bike & Walking Trail along the Frankton Arm of the lake. Stop at the Queenstown Bay beach area for a swim if the weather is warm (Lake Wakatipu is cold but refreshing in November). Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entry area to see the aviaries from outside, or splash out ~NZD $49 for full entry if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump at The World Bar or Pub on Wharf - both offer happy hour deals on drinks (~NZD $7-9 pints). For dinner, try Vudu Larder & Cafe for affordable, wholesome meals (~NZD $15-20) or grab fish and chips from Fishbone Bar & Grill takeaway window (~NZD $12-16).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at accommodation before departure (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kawarau Bungy Centre viewing area or nearby (~NZD $4-6 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Fish and chips from Fishbone takeaway or affordable pub meal (~NZD $12-20)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bungy Jump well in advance online at bungy.co.nz to secure your preferred time slot and potentially save with early bird pricing. Wear comfortable, secure clothing - no loose items. Weight restrictions apply (min 35kg, max 230kg). Video and photo packages available at extra cost (~NZD $30-50) - worth considering as a memento!

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Glenorchy - take the free Ritchies bus or arrange a carpool/rideshare (~NZD $15-20 return) along one of New Zealand's most scenic roads beside Lake Wakatipu (45min each way). Glenorchy is the gateway to the famous Routeburn and Greenstone tracks. Walk the free Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours return, flat and easy) through wetlands with views of snow-capped peaks and Paradise Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Glenorchy township (tiny but charming), grab a coffee at the Glenorchy Cafe (~NZD $5-6), and walk to the Glenorchy Wharf for stunning lake and mountain views. Attempt the lower section of the Paradise Road walk through beech forest (Lord of the Rings filming location) - free and accessible on foot. Return to Queenstown by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Queenstown, cook dinner at the accommodation using supermarket supplies (pasta, vegetables, canned goods ~NZD $8-12 for two). Rest your legs and plan the next days hiking adventures. Review weather forecasts for the coming days and adjust plans accordingly.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Glenorchy Wharf with mountain views (~NZD $4-6 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or stir-fry at accommodation (~NZD $8-12)

day_by_day.notes: The road from Queenstown to Glenorchy is 46km of winding lakeside road - absolutely stunning in November with wildflowers blooming. Check if the Routeburn Track day walk sections are accessible. Glenorchy has very limited services so bring everything you need from Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Tackle the Ben Lomond Track - Queenstown's most iconic and challenging day hike. Start early (07:00) from the Queenstown Gondola base area (10 min walk from town). Hike up through pine forest to the Skyline area, then continue on the Ben Lomond Track past the saddle to the summit at 1748m. The full return hike is approximately 11km and takes 5-7 hours. The 360-degree summit views are absolutely breathtaking on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond descent, taking your time on the steep sections. Stop at the saddle for lunch with panoramic views. Descend back through the forest to Queenstown. Alternatively, if you took the Gondola up (~NZD $42 return - skip this to save money and hike all the way), ride it back down. Total elevation gain approximately 1400m.
day_by_day.evening: Reward yourself after a huge day with a well-deserved meal. Try Bao Now for cheap and cheerful Asian street food (~NZD $10-14) or Winnies Pizza for affordable wood-fired pizza slices (~NZD $8-12). Soak your tired legs in a hot shower and get an early night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hearty breakfast before the big hike - oats with banana and honey (~NZD $3-4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Ben Lomond saddle or summit - energy bars, sandwiches, nuts, fruit (~NZD $5-7 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Bao Now or Winnies Pizza in Queenstown town centre (~NZD $10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a serious alpine hike - only attempt in good weather. Check MetService forecast the night before. Carry minimum 2L water, sunscreen, warm layers (temperature drops significantly near summit), and a rain jacket. The track is well-marked but steep. Start early to avoid afternoon thunderstorms which can build in summer. This is one of the best free hikes in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning after Ben Lomond. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and do laundry at the accommodation or nearby laundromat (~NZD $6-8). Spend the morning exploring the free Queenstown Arts Centre and browsing the local shops and galleries on Beach Street and the Mall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free Queenstown Trail walk to Arthurs Point (~5km each way along the Shotover River). This flat, easy riverside trail is perfect for tired legs. Explore the historic Arthurs Point area where gold was discovered in the 1860s. Dip your feet in the Shotover River if conditions are safe. Return along the same trail or arrange a pickup.
day_by_day.evening: Friday night in Queenstown - explore the vibrant nightlife on a budget. Start with happy hour at The Pub on Wharf or Smiths Craft Beer House (~NZD $7-8 craft beers). For dinner, try the affordable ramen or noodle bowls at Bao Now or grab a cheap kebab from one of the late-night spots on Shotover Street (~NZD $10-14).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered relaxed breakfast at accommodation - toast, eggs, coffee (~NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and fruit eaten along the Arthurs Point trail (~NZD $3-5)
meals.dinner: Affordable ramen or kebab in Queenstown town centre (~NZD $10-14)

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned recovery day - listen to your body after the demanding Ben Lomond hike. Use the afternoon to plan and book ahead for the Milford Sound day trip (Day 8) if not already arranged. Check bus/tour prices and book early for best rates. Milford Sound bus tours from Queenstown start from ~NZD $99-130.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arrowtown - take the Connectabus from Queenstown (~NZD $5-7 each way, 30 min) to this beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush village. Explore the free Arrow River Bridges Trail (2.5 hours, 8km loop) through stunning schist rock gorges and historic Chinese settlement ruins. The trail follows the Arrow River through willow trees and dramatic rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Back in Arrowtown, visit the free Lakes District Museum to learn about gold rush history. Walk the short Tobins Track lookout (45 min return) for elevated views over the village and Wakatipu basin. Browse the charming main street. If feeling adventurous, try gold panning in the Arrow River (free - bring a pan or borrow one from the museum).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by late afternoon. Saturday evening - cook a celebratory dinner at the accommodation or treat yourself to a meal at Rata restaurant (slightly splurge but worth it for a special occasion ~NZD $25-35 mains) or stick to budget with a meal from the Queenstown Supermarket deli counter (~NZD $8-12).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before catching the bus (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten along the Arrow River trail or at the riverside picnic area (~NZD $4-6)
meals.dinner: Self-catered or budget deli meal at accommodation (~NZD $8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is particularly beautiful in November with spring wildflowers blooming along the Arrow River. The Connectabus timetable is limited on weekends - check times carefully before departure and plan your return journey. The Arrow River Bridges Trail is one of the most underrated free walks in the Queenstown area.

day_by_day.morning: MILFORD SOUND DAY TRIP - The most iconic experience in New Zealand! Depart Queenstown very early (~05:30-06:00) on a budget day tour bus (~NZD $99-130 including cruise, book in advance). The 5-hour drive through Te Anau and the stunning Homer Tunnel is itself spectacular. Stop at Mirror Lakes and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound and board a 2-hour scenic cruise through the fiord (~NZD $75-85 if not included in tour package). See the iconic Mitre Peak (1692m), Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins. The scale of the sheer rock walls plunging into the dark fiord waters is truly humbling. Begin the long drive back to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown around 20:00-21:00 (it's a very long day!). Grab a quick, easy dinner - pick up a pre-made meal from the supermarket or order a cheap takeaway pizza (~NZD $12-16). Get to bed early as you'll be exhausted from the 15+ hour day.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before 05:30 departure - pre-prepared the night before (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the Milford Sound cruise or at the Milford Sound wharf area (~NZD $5-8 self-prepared - bring enough food as Milford Sound cafe prices are very high)
meals.dinner: Quick supermarket meal or cheap takeaway pizza upon return to Queenstown (~NZD $10-15)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Book the Milford Sound tour well in advance - it sells out, especially in summer. Bring layers as Milford Sound can be cold and wet even in November (it receives over 7 metres of rain per year). Rain actually makes the fiord more dramatic with hundreds of temporary waterfalls. Bring motion sickness tablets if prone to seasickness. The day is very long (~15 hours) but absolutely worth it - Milford Sound is one of the world's great natural wonders.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the long Milford Sound day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow start. After breakfast, take the free Queenstown Hill Walk (shorter version - just to the Basket of Dreams sculpture, 30 min return) for gentle morning exercise with lake views. Alternatively, simply sit at the lakefront and enjoy the view with a coffee from a local cafe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Queenstown Botanic Gardens thoroughly - often overlooked but beautiful in November with spring blooms. Then walk the easy Queenstown Bay to Frankton Arm lakeside path (3km, 45 min, flat). Visit the free Queenstown i-SITE to pick up information about the remaining days. Spend time planning and booking any remaining activities.
day_by_day.evening: Try a new budget dining experience - head to the Queenstown Night Market (check current schedule) or try Eichardt's Bar for their famous happy hour deals. Cook dinner at accommodation using leftover supermarket supplies. Spend the evening researching the Kepler Track or Routeburn Track options for upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered relaxed breakfast - treat yourself to fresh fruit and yogurt (~NZD $4-6)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap and cheerful $10 lunch special from one of the cafes along the Queenstown Mall (~NZD $10-12)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation or Night Market (~NZD $8-15)

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to do any necessary admin - charge all devices, back up photos from Milford Sound, repack bags, and do laundry. Check the weather forecast for the next 3-4 days to plan hiking activities. Research the Kepler Track day walk from Te Anau as a potential day trip option.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Wanaka - take the InterCity bus or Ritchies shuttle (~NZD $15-25 each way, 1 hour) to the beautiful lakeside town of Wanaka. Start with the famous free Rob Roy Glacier Track - but note this requires a car to reach the Matukituki Valley trailhead. Instead, walk the free Mount Iron Track from Wanaka township (1.5 hours return, 240m elevation gain) for stunning 360-degree views over Lake Wanaka, Lake Hawea, and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the free Wanaka lakefront promenade and visit the iconic That Wanaka Tree (a lone willow tree growing in the lake - one of New Zealand's most photographed spots). Explore the Wanaka town centre and browse the shops. Visit the free Rippon Vineyard viewpoint for stunning lake and mountain views (no tasting required). Enjoy a swim at the Wanaka lakefront beach if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Grab dinner in Wanaka before catching the evening bus back to Queenstown. Try Francesca's Italian Kitchen for affordable pasta (~NZD $18-22) or grab fish and chips from the lakefront takeaway (~NZD $10-14). Return to Queenstown by 20:00-21:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before bus departure (~NZD $2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Wanaka lakefront with views of That Wanaka Tree (~NZD $4-6 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Fish and chips at Wanaka lakefront or affordable pasta restaurant (~NZD $10-22)

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a slightly smaller, quieter alternative to Queenstown with a more relaxed vibe. Check bus timetables carefully for return journeys. The drive between Queenstown and Wanaka via the Crown Range Road (highest sealed road in NZ) is spectacular - try to sit on the right side of the bus for best views. November is a lovely time to visit with wildflowers blooming.

day_by_day.morning: One more big hike day - tackle the Remarkables Ski Area Loop Track. Take the Remarkables Ski Area Road (accessible via rideshare or taxi ~NZD $25-35 each way) to the ski area base at 1600m. From there, hike the free Lake Alta Track (3 hours return, relatively easy from the ski area base) to a stunning alpine lake nestled in the Remarkables Range with dramatic rocky peaks reflected in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Remarkables area - the Shadow Basin Walk offers additional alpine scenery (add 1-2 hours). Alternatively, if road access is an issue, do the lower Remarkables Track from the valley floor (longer but free to access). Descend and return to Queenstown by mid-afternoon. Stop at the Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge viewpoint (free) on the way back for river views.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner in Queenstown - treat yourself slightly after days of budget eating. Try Rata restaurant for a special meal (~NZD $25-35 mains) or Flame Bar & Grill for a mid-range steak (~NZD $28-35). Alternatively, splurge on a Fergburger meal deal with loaded fries (~NZD $20-25) as a true Queenstown send-off.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hearty breakfast before hiking (~NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Alta with Remarkables views (~NZD $5-8 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Slight splurge dinner at Rata or Flame Bar & Grill (~NZD $28-40) as a treat

day_by_day.notes: The Remarkables Ski Area Road is only open to private vehicles with appropriate access - check current conditions and access rules. In November the ski area is not operating so access may be limited. Alternatively, substitute this with the Coronet Peak Track (accessible from Arthurs Point) which offers similar alpine scenery. Always check weather conditions before alpine hikes.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day - start with a relaxed morning walk along the Queenstown lakefront one last time. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE for any last-minute souvenirs or information. Browse the Remarkable Sweet Shop for affordable NZ-made chocolates and candies as gifts (~NZD $5-15). Take the free Queenstown Bay Walk one final time to soak in the incredible scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: if budget allows and you still have adrenaline to spare, consider the Shotover Canyon Swing (~NZD $189) or Nevis Swing (~NZD $165) for one final adventure. Budget alternative: hike the One Mile Creek Track (2 hours return, free) through native bush starting from the Queenstown town centre. Pack and organise bags for departure. Do a final supermarket run for any remaining supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Queenstown dinner - return to Fergburger for the full experience if you haven't already, or try The Cow Restaurant for affordable wood-fired pizza in a cosy stone cottage atmosphere (~NZD $18-24). Take a final sunset walk along the lakefront and up to the Queenstown Gardens for one last look at The Remarkables reflected in Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast - use up remaining accommodation food supplies (~NZD $2-4)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap pie or sandwich from a local bakery for a quintessential NZ experience (~NZD $5-8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Fergburger or The Cow Restaurant (~NZD $18-25)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to back up all photos, charge all devices, and prepare for departure. Check out procedures for Queenstown Boutique Stay and confirm any luggage storage options if needed. Exchange any remaining NZD cash. Write down favourite memories and recommendations for fellow travellers!

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Wake up early, enjoy a final self-catered breakfast, and complete check-out from Queenstown Boutique Stay. Depending on your departure flight time, take one last walk to the Queenstown lakefront to say goodbye to The Remarkables. The Connectabus to Queenstown Airport departs regularly from the town centre (~NZD $10, 15-20 min journey) - check timetables the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Queenstown Airport with plenty of time before your flight. Browse the airport shops for last-minute NZ souvenirs (Whittakers chocolate is excellent value). Reflect on an incredible 13 days exploring the South Island - from the world's first commercial bungy jump to epic hikes, Milford Sound, and some of the most dramatic scenery on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Departure - farewell New Zealand South Island!

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast using remaining supplies (~NZD $2-4)
meals.lunch: Airport cafe or bring packed snacks for the journey (~NZD $8-15)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport is small but busy - arrive at least 2 hours before domestic flights and 3 hours before international flights. Biosecurity rules are strict in NZ - dispose of any fruit, nuts, or plant materials before going through airport security. The Connectabus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately NZD $800-1100 per person for 13 days including the Bungy Jump (~NZD $175) and Milford Sound tour (~NZD $130).

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, clear customs, and transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay (~20 min). Check in, freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront and Steamer Wharf to get your bearings. Browse the town center and pick up any supplies needed for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant restaurant scene along Beach Street and the Mall. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Fergbaker (iconic local bakery) — grab a pie or sandwich for a quick, affordable bite after landing.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant — mid-range farm-to-table New Zealand cuisine in a warm, stylish setting. Budget approx. NZD $45–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm all upcoming bookings (Nevis Bungy, Routeburn Track huts, Milford Sound) from your hotel. Pick up a NZ SIM card at the airport if needed. November is late spring in NZ — expect long daylight hours (sunset ~9 pm) and mild temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump (43m) — Book the 9:00–10:00 am slot with AJ Hackett. Located just 23km from Queenstown (~25 min drive), this is the world's first commercial bungy site above the stunning Kawarau River Gorge. An adrenaline-packed start to your South Island adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bungy, drive back through Gibbston Valley wine country. Stop at Gibbston Valley Winery for a cave wine tasting and a light lunch on their terrace. Return to Queenstown and rent a bike or join a guided e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail along Lake Hayes.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Queenstown Hill for a sunset walk (1.5 hrs return) with panoramic views over the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu. Descend into town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or visit Vudu Cafe & Larder — excellent eggs, pastries, and coffee. Budget NZD $18–25.
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery restaurant — shared platters with local cheeses, charcuterie, and wine. Budget NZD $30–45 per person.
meals.dinner: Bespoke Kitchen — wholesome, fresh dinner bowls and mains in a relaxed setting. Budget NZD $25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bungy must be pre-booked online via AJ Hackett website. Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes. Gibbston Valley is en route back to Queenstown — no detour needed. Bring a light jacket for the evening hill walk.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump (134m) — New Zealand's highest bungy jump. AJ Hackett operates transfers from their Queenstown base (~9:00 am departure). The cable car ride over the Nevis Valley alone is breathtaking. This is a serious bucket-list experience — allow 4–5 hours total including transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Recover with a relaxing walk along the lakefront promenade or a short scenic gondola ride up Bob's Peak for views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Visit the Skyline complex and enjoy the luge if energy permits.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Queenstown followed by a stroll through the lively town center. Queenstown has an excellent craft beer scene — visit Altitude Brewing taproom for post-adventure drinks.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the Nevis transfer — fuel up well.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or grab food at the AJ Hackett base before departure. Alternatively, eat at Skyline's casual café on return.
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill — excellent fresh seafood and New Zealand lamb in a mid-range setting. Budget NZD $40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy transfers depart from AJ Hackett's downtown Queenstown station — confirm exact departure time when booking. Weight and health restrictions apply — check AJ Hackett's website. The Nevis is significantly more intense than Kawarau; doing Kawarau first (Day 2) was intentional to build confidence.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after two big bungy days. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, then explore the Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market (held Saturdays and Sundays — if timing aligns) or browse local galleries. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful morning walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Arrowtown (~25 min from Queenstown) — a beautifully preserved 19th-century gold rush town. Walk the Arrow River Gorge Trail (2 hrs, easy–moderate), explore the Chinese Settlement historic site, and browse the charming boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Arrowtown before returning to Queenstown, or head back to Queenstown for dinner. Arrowtown has some excellent restaurant options worth staying for.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast or nearby café — try Vudu Cafe or Bespoke Kitchen.
meals.lunch: Provisions of Arrowtown — a beloved local deli and café with excellent sandwiches, salads, and baked goods. Budget NZD $15–25.
meals.dinner: The Chop Shop Food Merchants (Arrowtown) or return to Queenstown for Habebe's — Middle Eastern-inspired dishes, great value. Budget NZD $25–40.

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is deliberately lighter to allow physical recovery before the Routeburn Track multi-day hike beginning Day 5. Use the afternoon to pack your Routeburn gear: layers, rain jacket, hiking boots, snacks, and hut sleeping bag liner. Confirm Great Walks hut bookings via DOC (Department of Conservation).

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 1. Depart Queenstown early (~7:00 am) by shuttle or rental car to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (~1.5 hrs drive). Begin hiking from the Routeburn Shelter end. Morning section: Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats Hut (2.5 hrs, 7.5km, gentle terrain through beech forest alongside the Routeburn River).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats Hut to Routeburn Falls Hut (1.5 hrs, 2.5km, steeper climb with spectacular waterfall views). Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut — one of New Zealand's most scenic Great Walks huts. Explore the area around the hut, including views up toward Harris Saddle.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut. Cook dinner using your packed supplies or hut facilities. Socialize with fellow hikers, enjoy the sunset over the valley from the hut deck.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or packed breakfast to eat at the trailhead.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the trail — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, nuts.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Routeburn Falls Hut — bring freeze-dried meals, instant noodles, or pre-prepared food. Hot water available at the hut.

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track Great Walks hut bookings are ESSENTIAL and must be made in advance via the DOC website (doc.govt.nz). November is peak season — book months ahead. Shuttle transfers from Queenstown to Routeburn Shelter available via Tracknet or Queenstown Connections. Pack light but include: rain gear, warm layers, first aid kit, headlamp, and trekking poles (recommended). Huts provide mattresses — bring a sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 2. Early start from Routeburn Falls Hut. Climb to Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the highest point of the Routeburn Track with extraordinary panoramic views of Fiordland and the Darran Mountains. Optional: side trip to Conical Hill summit (45 min return) for even more dramatic views on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle to Lake Mackenzie Hut (3–4 hrs from Falls Hut total, 11km). The descent reveals stunning Lake Mackenzie — a turquoise glacial lake surrounded by ancient beech forest. Swim in the lake if weather permits (it will be cold!). Rest and explore around the hut.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Lake Mackenzie Hut. This is one of the most beautiful hut locations in New Zealand — enjoy the golden evening light on the lake and mountains. Cook dinner and rest well for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Routeburn Falls Hut — oats, muesli, instant coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — eaten at Harris Saddle with incredible views.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Lake Mackenzie Hut — freeze-dried meals or pre-packed food.

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and cold even in November — always carry full rain gear and a warm layer regardless of morning weather. If the weather is poor at the saddle, visibility may be limited but the hike is still stunning. The DOC ranger at Routeburn Falls Hut can advise on conditions each morning. Distance today: approximately 11km, 5–6 hours of hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 3. Final section: Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (8.5km, 3–4 hrs). Hike through ancient beech forest, passing the Earland Falls (174m waterfall — one of the tallest on the track). Arrive at The Divide — the lowest pass in the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pre-arranged shuttle from The Divide back to Queenstown (~2 hrs). Arrive Queenstown mid-afternoon. Check back into Queenstown Boutique Stay. Shower, do laundry, and decompress after three days on the track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track with a proper sit-down dinner in Queenstown. Treat yourself — you've earned it.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Lake Mackenzie Hut — last trail breakfast.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at The Divide or eat at the small shelter while waiting for the shuttle.
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery — upscale-casual lakefront restaurant with excellent New Zealand beef and lamb. Budget NZD $50–75 per person. A well-deserved treat.

day_by_day.notes: Book return shuttle from The Divide to Queenstown in advance via Tracknet or similar operator — schedules are limited. Confirm your hotel reservation is still active. The Divide is also a junction for the Milford Sound road, which is relevant for Day 11. Total Routeburn Track distance: ~32km over 3 days — a genuine achievement. Allow time to rest on Day 8.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market (held Sunday mornings at Earnslaw Park) for local produce, artisan goods, and excellent street food — a great way to experience local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional light activity: rent a kayak or paddleboard on Lake Wakatipu (~2 hrs), or take the TSS Earnslaw vintage steamship cruise across the lake to Walter Peak High Country Farm (includes a farm show and afternoon tea). A relaxed, scenic afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's bar and live music scene. The town is lively on Sunday evenings — visit Atlas Beer Café or Zephyr Bar for craft beers and a relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Queenstown Farmers Market — fresh pastries, local honey, artisan coffee. Budget NZD $10–20.
meals.lunch: Yonder — excellent casual dining with creative New Zealand-inspired dishes. Budget NZD $25–35.
meals.dinner: Pub-style dinner at The World Bar or Minus 5° Ice Bar experience followed by a casual meal at Winnies Pizza. Budget NZD $25–40.

day_by_day.notes: Today is a genuine rest and recovery day — your body needs it after the Routeburn Track. Avoid any strenuous activity. Use the afternoon to research and confirm logistics for the Milford Sound trip (Days 10–11) and plan the Te Anau overnight stay. Check weather forecasts for the Milford Sound region.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Te Anau (~2 hrs, 170km). Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check into your Te Anau accommodation (book a mid-range option like Te Anau Lodge or Fiordland Hotel). Morning arrival — walk along the beautiful Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a magical 2-hour guided tour by boat across Lake Te Anau to ancient limestone caves filled with glowworms. Book in advance through Real Journeys. Alternatively, explore the DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the region's ecology and geology.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Te Anau township — a small but charming town with a good selection of restaurants. Early dinner and early bed, as Day 10 starts very early for the Milford Sound journey.

meals.breakfast: Final Queenstown hotel breakfast before departure, or stop at Miles Better Pies in Mossburn (~45 min from Queenstown) — legendary NZ pies.
meals.lunch: Redcliff Restaurant & Bar (Te Anau) — excellent casual lunch with Fiordland venison and local specialties. Budget NZD $25–40.
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck Restaurant (Te Anau) — popular mid-range restaurant with great pizza, pasta, and local seafood. Budget NZD $30–50.

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves tours depart from Te Anau township — book in advance via Real Journeys (realjourneys.co.nz). The Milford Road (SH94) from Te Anau to Milford Sound is one of the world's great scenic drives — you'll travel this road tomorrow. Fill up with petrol in Te Anau as there are no fuel stops on the Milford Road. Set an early alarm for Day 10.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise — Day 1. Depart Te Anau very early (~6:00–7:00 am) to drive the spectacular Milford Road (SH94, 120km, ~2 hrs). Stop at the Mirror Lakes, Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain, and the Homer Tunnel along the way. Arrive at Milford Sound and join your guided walk along the Milford Track day walk section.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board your Milford Sound scenic cruise. Sail through the dramatic fiord with towering peaks rising 1,200m from the water, cascading waterfalls (Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls), and abundant wildlife — fur seals, dolphins, and penguins are commonly spotted. The cruise lasts approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back from Milford Sound to Te Anau (~2 hrs). Arrive Te Anau early evening. Dinner in Te Anau and overnight stay.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or eat at the hotel before the 6:00 am departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch to eat at Milford Sound between the walk and cruise — there is a café at the Milford Sound visitor complex if needed.
meals.dinner: Sandfly Cafe (Te Anau) — casual, popular local café with good evening meals. Budget NZD $20–35.

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound guided walk and cruise must be pre-booked. Multiple operators run this combination — try Real Journeys or Go Orange. The Milford Road is subject to closures due to rock falls and avalanche control — check NZTA road conditions the evening before (journeys.nzta.govt.nz). Sandflies at Milford Sound are notoriously fierce — bring insect repellent. November weather at Milford Sound can be wet (it receives over 7 meters of rain annually), but rain actually makes the waterfalls more spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau back toward Queenstown, but detour south to visit the Mavora Lakes (approx. 35km off SH94 on a gravel road) — a stunning and remote wilderness area used as a filming location in Lord of the Rings. Short walk around North Mavora Lake (~1.5 hrs, easy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Kingston (~1.5 hrs from Mavora) and then back to Queenstown (~45 min). Arrive Queenstown mid-afternoon. Check back into Queenstown Boutique Stay. Alternatively, stop at Frankton for grocery shopping or visit the Remarkables Ski Area base (scenic views even in summer).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Visit the iconic Skyline Gondola for sunset views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables — one of the most beautiful sunsets in New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Te Anau before checkout.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mavora Lakes — a picnic in one of New Zealand's most remote and beautiful settings.
meals.dinner: Hawker & Roll (Queenstown) — delicious Southeast Asian-inspired street food. Budget NZD $20–30. Or try Vudu Larder for a relaxed evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Mavora Lakes road is gravel — drive carefully and check conditions. A standard rental car is fine in dry weather, but confirm with your rental company. The detour adds approximately 1.5–2 hours to the drive but is well worth it for the scenery and solitude. This is a good day for photography — the Mavora Lakes and Mavora Walkway are spectacularly beautiful and very uncrowded.

day_by_day.morning: Queenstown area hiking — Ben Lomond Track. Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak, then hike the Ben Lomond Track to the summit (1,748m). This is a serious day hike (8–9 hrs return from the gondola, or 11 hrs from town) — start by 8:00 am. The views from the summit are extraordinary — Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and on a clear day, as far as Fiordland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond summit hike — this is an all-day commitment. The track above the saddle involves some scrambling and can be exposed. Return to the gondola base by late afternoon. Alternatively, if a shorter option is preferred, hike only to Ben Lomond Saddle (4–5 hrs return from gondola) for still-spectacular views.
day_by_day.evening: Well-deserved rest and a celebratory final full-day dinner in Queenstown. Reflect on an incredible 12 days in the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Early, hearty breakfast at the hotel — fuel up well for the big hike.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the Ben Lomond Track — at the saddle or summit.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant (revisit) or try Amisfield Winery & Bistro (20 min from Queenstown near Lake Hayes) — outstanding seasonal NZ cuisine with wine pairing. Budget NZD $60–90 per person. A special final evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a serious alpine hike — check weather forecasts the night before and morning of. Do not attempt the summit in poor visibility or high winds. Carry: 2L+ water, snacks, full rain gear, warm layers, sunscreen, and a map/downloaded offline trail. The gondola operates from approximately 9:00 am — check current hours. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the descent. This is one of the best day hikes accessible from Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Checkout from Queenstown Boutique Stay. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy one last walk along the Queenstown waterfront or a coffee at your favourite café. Browse local shops for New Zealand souvenirs — Merino wool products, Manuka honey, and locally made crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Queenstown Airport for your departing flight. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Queenstown Airport is approximately 8km from the town center (~15 min drive).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown. Farewell to one of the world's most spectacular destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Queenstown breakfast — Bespoke Kitchen or Vudu Cafe for a memorable last meal. Budget NZD $20–30.
meals.lunch: Airport café or a final pie from Fergbaker before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your transit airport.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and work backwards to plan your morning. Queenstown Airport has limited parking — use a taxi, Uber, or pre-booked shuttle. Return your rental car before heading to the terminal if applicable. Declare any food items at customs. New Zealand has strict biosecurity — do not carry fresh fruit, meat, or plant material. Review your travel insurance documentation and ensure all gear is packed. This has been an incredible 13 days covering bungy jumping, multi-day hiking, fiords, and the best of the South Island — well done!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Day Hike
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's Great Walks, this iconic 19.4km hike traverses volcanic terrain, emerald lakes, and dramatic landscapes. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown to maximize daylight hours. Ideal for experienced hikers seeking breathtaking alpine scenery without wasting arrival day logistics.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett in the Nevis Valley. Located just 45 minutes from central Queenstown, this is the ultimate adrenaline experience. Book in advance to secure a morning slot and combine with nearby accommodation in Queenstown to avoid long transfers.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-renowned Great Walk spanning 32km through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Stay at huts along the trail to avoid costly transfers. Book hut passes well in advance. Starting from Glenorchy, just 45 minutes from Queenstown, this minimizes travel time and maximizes trail days.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungy site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, located just 23km from central Queenstown. A historic and accessible experience perfect for first-timers or those wanting a shorter transfer. Combine with a riverside café lunch nearby to make the most of the afternoon.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise
experiences.description: Combine a guided hike along the Milford Track day walk with a scenic cruise through Milford Sound's dramatic fiords and waterfalls. Depart from Te Anau (2.5 hours from Queenstown) and stay overnight in Te Anau to avoid a rushed same-day return. This keeps costs low while delivering maximum natural impact.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Private transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll along the Queenstown waterfront and Steamer Wharf precinct to get acquainted with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset gondola ride up Bob's Peak on the Skyline Gondola for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Dinner at the summit restaurant or descend for a fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light arrival meal at Queenstown Airport or a quick bite at Vudu Cafe & Larder on arrival
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — celebrated farm-to-table cuisine with stunning vineyard views just outside Queenstown; book the Trust the Chef degustation menu

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump — the world's first commercial bungy site, 43 meters above the Kawarau River, just 23km from Queenstown. An iconic and historic adrenaline experience to kick off the adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and explore Arrowtown, a charming historic gold-rush village 20 minutes away. Wander the heritage lanes, visit the Lakes District Museum, and browse boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic Lake Wakatipu sunset cruise aboard a private charter or the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship. Return to Queenstown for dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — request a full cooked spread
meals.lunch: The Chop Shop Food Merchants in Arrowtown — artisan sandwiches and local produce
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Chef Josh Emett — one of Queenstown's finest, showcasing New Zealand produce with contemporary flair

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bungy through AJ Hackett well in advance. Check weight and health requirements. Wear comfortable clothing for the jump. GoPro footage packages available on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters, suspended above the dramatic Nevis Valley gorge. A private 4WD transfer from Queenstown takes you to the remote valley. An absolute bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Relax and recover with a luxury spa treatment at a premium Queenstown day spa (e.g., Eforea Spa at Hilton or Spa at Millbrook Resort).
day_by_day.evening: Private wine tasting session at a Central Otago cellar door — arrange a guided tasting of world-class Pinot Noir at Peregrine Wines or Chard Farm with a sommelier.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the jump
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet hamper arranged by the hotel to enjoy near the Nevis Valley (coordinate with AJ Hackett or the hotel concierge)
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery Queenstown — premium steaks and New Zealand lamb in an elegant lakeside setting

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy requires a full morning. The transfer alone is an adventure. No loose items permitted during the jump. Spa booking should be made in advance. Two major bungy jumps back-to-back — ensure you're well-rested and hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 on trail. Private transfer or guided shuttle to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Hike from the Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats Hut (approx. 7.5km, 2–3 hours). Enjoy lush beech forest and river valley scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (approx. 2.5km, 1.5 hours). Dramatic waterfall views and alpine meadows. Settle into the premium lodge-style hut accommodation (book private rooms through DOC's Great Walks system).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Routeburn Falls Hut overlooking the valley. Prepare a gourmet packed dinner (arranged by the hotel or a Queenstown caterer) or enjoy hut facilities. Stargazing in a pristine dark sky environment.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack prepared by the hotel — artisan bread, charcuterie, local cheeses, fruit
meals.dinner: Gourmet dehydrated premium meals or pre-packed catered dinner at Routeburn Falls Hut — coordinate with a guided hiking company for full catering service

day_by_day.notes: Book Routeburn Track Great Walk hut passes through DOC well in advance (opens months ahead). Consider booking a guided Routeburn experience through Ultimate Hikes for full catering, guiding, and private lodge accommodation. Pack rain gear — weather can change rapidly. November is shoulder season with generally good conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 2. Hike from Routeburn Falls Hut over Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the dramatic high point of the track with panoramic views across Fiordland. Approx. 11km to Lake Mackenzie Hut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut. Relax by the stunning glacial lake, swim if conditions allow, or take a short side trail to higher viewpoints. Rest and enjoy the extraordinary alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset reflections on Lake Mackenzie. Evening meal at the hut. Fellow hikers create a warm communal atmosphere. Early night to rest for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Routeburn Falls Hut — oats, coffee, and energy-rich foods
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch on the saddle — energy bars, nuts, sandwiches
meals.dinner: Premium catered dinner at Lake Mackenzie Hut — if using Ultimate Hikes guided service, full hot meals are provided

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and windy — layer appropriately. If weather is severe, rangers may advise on conditions. The view from Conical Hill (30-min side trip from Harris Saddle) is unmissable on a clear day.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 3 (final day). Hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (approx. 9km, 3–4 hours) through ancient beech forest and the Hollyford Valley. Complete the full 32km Great Walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shuttle transfer from The Divide back to Queenstown (approx. 2.5 hours). Return to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Hot shower, laundry service, and full relaxation. Optional: afternoon massage at a local spa.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track.

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast — hot drinks and hearty fuel for the last leg
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the final stretch
meals.dinner: Jervois Steak House Queenstown — premium celebration dinner with New Zealand grass-fed beef and fine wine

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate shuttle pickup from The Divide in advance. Luggage can be stored at the hotel or arranged for transfer separately if using a guided service. Allow time for recovery — hot bath and rest are recommended after three days on trail.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel. Optional gentle morning walk along the Queenstown Gardens lakefront track (flat, easy 3km loop) to stretch legs without stress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic helicopter flight over The Remarkables, Fiordland, and Mount Aspiring National Park — a premium way to appreciate the landscapes just hiked from a bird's-eye perspective. Many operators offer 30–60 minute scenic flights from Queenstown Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury shopping in Queenstown's premium boutiques for New Zealand merino wool, pounamu (greenstone) jewellery, and local art. Pre-dinner cocktails at the Eichardt's Private Hotel Bar — one of New Zealand's finest.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Pier 19 or Madam Woo Queenstown — relaxed waterfront dining
meals.dinner: Eichardt's Private Hotel — The Grille restaurant for an intimate, world-class dining experience overlooking Lake Wakatipu

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights should be booked in advance through operators like Over The Top Helicopters or Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters. Weather-dependent — have a backup activity ready.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or private transfer to Te Anau (approx. 2 hours from Queenstown). Check in at a premium Te Anau lodge (e.g., Fiordland Lodge). Morning walk along the Te Anau lakefront and explore the small town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour — a guided boat journey across Lake Te Anau to the ancient limestone caves, featuring thousands of glowworms in an underground grotto. A magical and unique experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset over Lake Te Anau from the lodge. Quiet evening in preparation for the Milford Sound day ahead.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Redcliff Restaurant Te Anau — charming heritage cottage restaurant with excellent New Zealand cuisine
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge dining room — intimate, lodge-style fine dining with Fiordland views

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau serves as the gateway to Milford Sound. Book glowworm caves in advance through Real Journeys. Fiordland Lodge is one of the most celebrated luxury lodges in New Zealand — highly recommended for this leg of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Te Anau toward Milford Sound (approx. 2 hours drive along one of the world's most scenic highways). Stop at Mirror Lakes, The Chasm, and Homer Tunnel for photography. Begin the Milford Track day walk — guided hike along a section of the famous Milford Track through ancient rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a premium small-group cruise through Milford Sound (Piopiotahi). Witness Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls. Watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins. Opt for an underwater observatory visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau. Relaxed evening at Fiordland Lodge with a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or lodge breakfast before 7am departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch on the Milford Track or onboard the cruise
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge — chef's tasting menu with paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Milford Sound cruise through Jucy Cruise or Real Journeys — select a premium small-vessel option for a more intimate experience. The drive to Milford Sound is itself a highlight — allow extra time for stops. Sandflies are notorious at Milford — bring quality insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike from Te Anau — Kepler Track day walk section (Lake Te Anau to Brod Bay, approx. 6km return). Beautiful beech forest and lakeside scenery without the commitment of the full Great Walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown. Stop at Kingston for photos of the historic Kingston Flyer railway. Continue to Arrowtown for a revisit or explore the Gibbston Valley wine region with a private cellar door tour and tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Queenstown. Check back into Queenstown Boutique Stay.

meals.breakfast: Fiordland Lodge breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery Restaurant — exceptional food paired with estate wines in a stunning schist stone setting
meals.dinner: The Sherwood Queenstown — sustainable, locally sourced menu in a relaxed but premium setting

day_by_day.notes: Gibbston Valley Winery cave tour is highly recommended — a unique wine tasting experience inside a natural rock cave. Book in advance. This is a more relaxed travel day after the intensity of Milford Sound.

day_by_day.morning: Guided e-bike or mountain bike tour through the Queenstown Trail network — explore the Gibbston Valley and Arrow River trails on a premium guided ride. A fantastic way to experience the landscape with less physical demand than hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Wakatipu jet boat experience — a thrilling high-speed jet boat ride through the Shotover Canyon or Kawarau River gorge. Operators like Shotover Jet offer premium experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury evening at leisure. Optional: Queenstown Casino for entertainment, or a private cocktail masterclass arranged through the hotel.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Cargo Brewbar Queenstown — waterfront craft beer and gourmet burgers
meals.dinner: Sasso Italian Restaurant Queenstown — refined Italian cuisine with premium New Zealand ingredients and an outstanding wine list

day_by_day.notes: E-bike tours can be arranged through Queenstown Bike Hire or guided operators. Jet boating is weather-dependent but rarely cancelled. This day balances adventure with a slightly more relaxed pace.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day guided hike in Mount Aspiring National Park — a private guided alpine hike to Rob Roy Glacier near Wanaka (approx. 2.5 hours drive from Queenstown). The Rob Roy Track (10km return) offers spectacular glacier, waterfall, and alpine meadow scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Wanaka town — visit the iconic 'That Wanaka Tree' on the lakefront, browse galleries, and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this stunning alpine lake town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Final evening in Queenstown — take time to revisit favourite spots or simply enjoy the lakefront.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast before departure to Wanaka
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Rob Roy Valley — gourmet hamper arranged by the hotel or guide
meals.dinner: Bistro Gentil Wanaka (if dining in Wanaka before returning) or Kappa Japanese Restaurant Queenstown for a change of cuisine — premium omakase-style experience

day_by_day.notes: Rob Roy Glacier hike requires a 4WD vehicle to reach the trailhead (Raspberry Creek). Arrange a private guided experience through a Wanaka-based operator. November conditions are generally excellent with wildflowers in bloom. Allow a full day for this excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute shopping for premium New Zealand souvenirs — merino wool products, manuka honey, pounamu jewellery, local wines. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final lakeside walk or coffee at a favourite café. Private transfer to Queenstown Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the hotel — order the full spread as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Federal Diner Queenstown — a beloved local institution for a relaxed final lunch with great coffee and food
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if the flight departs late. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in. Consider purchasing a case of Central Otago Pinot Noir to take home — many wineries offer international shipping as an alternative.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
